The concordance takes a reference from the earlier literature (a number of Prandtl’s Verzeichnis A or B, a volume or an item of Kleinschnitzová, a page of Norlind’s Bilaga I, a record of the National Library, a shelfmark) and gives the entry it stands for in this edition and the place where the book is today. It is set out twice from this edition’s side, by work and by volume, and once from the side of each earlier catalogue, in that catalogue’s own order. Every table ends in the same two columns, This edition and Held today; a reference that answers to no entry says why.

Read from this edition by work 251 · by volume 76 · Prandtl A 58 · Prandtl B 29 · Kleinschnitzová 104 · Šolc 13 · Norlind 218 · National Library index 102 · retired keys 33 · all tables

Carried on the entries as given, in the column Other numbers of the first table: Zinner’s number on 77 entries, as Norlind’s entry gives it; VD16 on 2; GW on 2; ISTC on 1; Adams on 1; Durling on 1; Voit 2015 on 1; the letter in Tycho’s correspondence that attests the book on 16. The lists of Prusík 1901, Kukula 1906–07, Mortensen 1955 and Gingerich 2002 are not concorded number by number; the records of the register (§4) cite them where they attest a book.

Prandtl’s misprints and slips, as read against Prusík 1901 and Kleinschnitzová 1933:

  • A15 'FERNETIUS / Fernetii' for Fernelius (inherited from Studnička).
  • A27 Band XV constituents printed '(23, 10, 27)' for (28, 10, 27).
  • A30 Band XIX constituents printed '(30, 24)' for (30, 25).
  • A26 and A27 are one book (14 H 190); Band XV has two constituents.
  • A6 / Band IX is a doublet of A5 / Band VIII (Prusík’s ‘1548’).
  • A44 'Tubingae' for Oppenheim (Koebel) 1518.
  • A52 'libri tres' for libri tredecim; XXIII is a Sammelband, not an Einzelband.
  • A58 'Wittenberg' for Leipzig (Camerarius, Valentin Papst 1556).
  • XVI: Crusius inscription placed 'auf dem Titelblatt von 55' and dated 1673; it stands on the title of 54 (first in the volume) and is dated 5 August 1654, 1673 being the Chomutov catalogue entry.
  • XXII 'Einzelband' (a Sammelband of four Rantzau pieces); IV, XXVIII describe states that no longer existed in 1932 (the manuscript removed before 1901; the Christmann an adligat of Scheiner 1631 by 1901).
  • XXV: Per Hierta had died in 1924.

e-ging-apianus-cosmographia-1561Petrus Apianus, Cosmographia (1561 edition)18 October 2026A duplicate of Apianus, Petrus, Cosmographia (per Gemma Frisium) (1553) (Band II): Gingerich’s ‘1561 edition’ is the year stamped on that volume’s binding, not an edition.
e-kl-27bFederico Commandino, Federici Commandini Urbinatis Liber de horologiorum descriptione18 October 2026Commandino’s Liber de horologiorum descriptione is the second part of the Rome imprint of 1562 that carries Ptolemy’s De analemmate (Ptolemaeus, Claudius (ed. Federico Commandino), Liber de analemmate, a Federico Commandino instauratus; eiusdem Commandini Liber de horologiorum descriptione (1562), Kleinschnitzová 27:1); Šolc 2002 (p. 331) itemised it as a title, as he did the other parts of works retired on 18 October 2026. Neither Kleinschnitzová nor the library’s record lists it as a separate piece.
e-letter-braun-theatrumGeorg Braun & Frans Hogenberg, Theatrum urbium / Civitates orbis terrarum (the city-atlas; sought the further volumes)18 October 2026The fourth part of the Civitates orbis terrarum that was at Hven in December 1588 was Rantzau’s loan (Norlind 1926, p. 218, among the loans; Opera omnia VII, 386; Rantzau’s own copy is at Augsburg, Gebele 1926), and Norlind found no evidence that Tycho owned parts I–III; a borrowed book is outside this catalogue.
e-letter-munoz-novastellaJerónimo Muñoz (Munosius), Libro del nuevo cometa / De nova stella (Spanish, Valencia 1573)18 October 2026No document attests the book as Tycho’s: he asked Hagecius for Muñoz’s Spanish tract on the new star on 25 January 1590 (Opera omnia VII, 224); Hagecius answered on 1/11 June 1590 that he had his own copy, the author’s gift, and no one to translate it (VII, 251: ‘MUNNOSIJ libellum de nova stella Hispanico idiomate, ab ipsomet olim mihi missum et donatum, habeo, qui tamen eum Latinum faciat, habeo neminem’) and sent nothing; Tycho withdrew the request on 3 August 1590 (VII, 270), and the Progymnasmata say he never saw the text (III, 80). The store had read Hagecius’s letter as a gift.
e-norlind-hipparchus-aratiHipparchus (ed. princeps, Petrus Victorius), In Arati et Eudoxi Phaenomena libri III18 October 2026The same object as Hipparchus (ed. Petrus Victorius), the copy annotated by Joseph Justus Scaliger, In Arati et Eudoxi Phaenomena libri III (the Greek editio princeps, with Scaliger’s annotations) (1567) — the Victorius Hipparchus of 1567 with Scaliger’s annotations, requested in August 1598 (Opera omnia VIII, 102), acknowledged in March 1599 (VIII, 151) and still with the heirs when Kepler asked Jørgen Brahe for it in November 1624 (KGW XIX, no. 7) — entered twice; Norlind’s record and the Ripensis story move to the surviving entry.
e-orphan-wroclaw(unspecified), [Tychoniana reported at Wrocław University Library, Głombiowski 1955 — no title establishe18 October 2026The Wrocław ‘Tychonianum’ of Głombiowski 1955 is the Mechanica of 1598 that Tycho inscribed for Jakob Monau — an outgoing presentation copy carried in the census of that edition, not a book of the library.
e-prandtlA-06Archimedes, Archimedis Syracusani opera18 October 2026Prandtl’s Verzeichnis A no. 6 (Archimedes, Basel 1548, his Band IX) answers to no edition; it is read as a misdating of the Hervagius Archimedes of 1544 in Band VIII (Sign. 5 C 31), and no separate book is sought. Prusík 1901 (p. 200, group A no. 8) and Kukula 1906–07 (p. 23) dated 5 C 31 to 1548; Prandtl took his Band IX from Prusík and his Band VIII from Studnička, hence the double count (Sonderdruck pp. 11 and 14).
e-prandtlA-27Paduanus, Joannes, Viridarium Mathematicorum18 October 2026Prandtl’s A 26 ‘Joa. Paduani opera, Venetiis 1563’ (Band XIV, after Prusík 1901, p. 200) and A 27 ‘Viridarium Mathematicorum’ (Band XV, after Studnička 1901, p. 54) are one book, the Viridarium mathematicorum of 1563 at Sign. 14 H 190 (Kleinschnitzová no. 15; the library’s record); merged into Paduanus, Joannes, Viridarium mathematicorum (1563).
e-prandtlA-38Reinhold, Erasmus, Initium Canonum Prutenicorum18 October 2026Prandtl’s A 38 (Initium canonum Prutenicorum) and A 39 (Logistice scrupulorum), his Band XI, are the section titles of the second, title-less copy of Reinhold’s Prutenicae tabulae at Sign. 14 J 192 (Prusík 1901, p. 199, group A no. 5; Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 20, and under no. 18: ‘Brahe besass das Werk noch in einem zweiten Exemplare’), one work, carried as Reinhold, Erasmus, Prutenicae tabulae coelestium motuum (the Initium canonum Prutenicorum and the Logistice scrupulorum astronomicorum, the copy without its title) (1551 or 1562); the edition had merged Band XI into the Mansfeld copy 14 J 176.
e-prandtlA-39Reinhold, Erasmus, Logistice scrupulorum astronomicorum18 October 2026Prandtl’s A 38 (Initium canonum Prutenicorum) and A 39 (Logistice scrupulorum), his Band XI, are the section titles of the second, title-less copy of Reinhold’s Prutenicae tabulae at Sign. 14 J 192 (Prusík 1901, p. 199, group A no. 5; Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 20, and under no. 18: ‘Brahe besass das Werk noch in einem zweiten Exemplare’), one work, carried as Reinhold, Erasmus, Prutenicae tabulae coelestium motuum (the Initium canonum Prutenicorum and the Logistice scrupulorum astronomicorum, the copy without its title) (1551 or 1562); the edition had merged Band XI into the Mansfeld copy 14 J 176.
e-solc-fk15bAntimachus (dialogue)18 October 2026Šolc 2002 (p. 330) lists ‘Antimachus’ and ‘Nicomedes’ as two dialogues following the prints in Sign. 14 H 190; they are the interlocutors of Maurolico’s Cosmographia in tres dialogos (Venice 1543), the volume’s second print (Maurolycus, Franciscus, Cosmographia (1543)) — parts of a work, not works.
e-solc-fk15cNicomedes (dialogue)18 October 2026Šolc 2002 (p. 330) lists ‘Antimachus’ and ‘Nicomedes’ as two dialogues following the prints in Sign. 14 H 190; they are the interlocutors of Maurolico’s Cosmographia in tres dialogos (Venice 1543), the volume’s second print (Maurolycus, Franciscus, Cosmographia (1543)) — parts of a work, not works.
e-solc-fk21bBrevis explicatio doctrinae sinuum (followed by tables)18 October 2026Šolc 2002 (p. 330) lists ‘Brevis explicatio doctrinae sinuum followed by tables’ among the texts of Sign. 14 K 70; it is the sinus doctrine of Brucaeus’s De motu primo libri tres (Rostock 1573), the volume’s second print (Brucaeus, Henricus, Henrici Brucaei de motu primo libri tres (1573)) — a part of a work.

e-letter-leovitius-mssLeovitius, Cyprianus, Manuscripts at the Fugger Library: Ephemerides; Tabulae directionum resolutae; the great D20 October 2026A loan, not an acquisition: Herwart borrowed the Fugger manuscripts for Tycho and the entry's own note says he never owned them (Thoren, p. 421 n. 205); retired by the rule that retired the Braun Theatrum (a documented loan is not an entry).
